skill.description: Gives the method for one kind of job. `name` is what follows `skill` in the list of the skills.

name.description: The name in the list, like `web-research`

skill.answers: The text of the skill. An unknown name: `No skill named X. The skills are: …`, with the list.

terminal.description: Runs one command and returns what it prints. The shell is PowerShell 7 on Windows and starts in the project folder. For programs: python, git, bun, npm, tests. Files have their own commands: `search`, `read`, `write`, `edit`.

command.description: The command, as you would type it in PowerShell

folder.description: A folder of the project to run it in, like `src`. Without it: the project folder

wait.description: How many seconds to wait for it to end. Without it: 60. At most 600

background.description: true for a server or a program that must stay on: it answers with what was printed in the first seconds and leaves it running

terminal.answers: What the program printed, the last 200 lines, and `exit N` when N is not 0. Errors arrive in English, in one or two lines, without colour codes. When `wait` is over it stops the program and says so, naming `wait` and `background`. With `background`: what was printed in the first five seconds, and `Still running`; the program stops when the conversation is closed, and the app shows it to the user. A command that only lists, shows, finds or searches files (`ls`, `dir`, `cat`, `type`, `head`, `tail`, `pwd`, `find`, `grep`, `Get-ChildItem`, `Get-Content`, `Select-String`), in its plain forms: not run; `read` or `search` is run in its place and the answer is `Done with \`read notes.txt\`:` and what that command answers. The same command with an option that asks for something else (`grep -c`, a pattern, `find -type d`, several files) runs in the shell as it is. `cd` alone: not run, saying that every command starts in the project folder and naming `folder`; `cd X && command`: the command is run in X. A path of another computer, like `/workspace/src`, in `folder` or in a command that only shows or finds files: taken from the project folder, and the answer says so. In a command that runs a program nothing is rewritten: a place outside the project named there (a whole path, `..`, `~`, a path of another computer) means the command is not run, refused with what the project folder holds. This reading of the command is not a fence: a place it does not recognise is not stopped. A whole path inside the project: run as it is.

read.description: Returns the text of a file, or the list of what a folder holds. The first line of the answer says which lines you got and how many the file has; everything after it is the file, each line with its number. Reads Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files as text.

path.description: The file or the folder, from the project folder: `notes.txt`, `src/app.js`, `.`

from.description: The first line to return. Without it: the first

lines.description: How many lines to return. Without it: 200

read.answers: A file: first `notes.txt, lines 1-200 of 540`, then those lines with their numbers, and nothing after the last line of the file. A folder: its files and folders, one per line, from the project folder. A Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF file: its text, with the titles of sheets and slides. Not found: `No file X. The folder holds: …`. A whole path inside the project: read, and shown from the project folder. A path of another computer, like `/workspace/notes.txt`: taken from the project folder, and the answer says so. Any other place outside the project: refused, with what the project folder holds.

write.description: Creates a file, or replaces a whole file, with the text you give. Makes the folders in its path if they are not there. For a page it answers with what the browser shows.

path.description: The file, from the project folder: `page.html`, `data/orders.csv`

content.description: The whole text of the file

write.answers: `Written X (N lines)`, with X from the project folder also when a whole path was given. A page (.html): then the page as `page_view` gives it, text, numbered links and buttons, errors of the console. A file that exists and that this conversation has not read to its last line: refused, saying which lines were read, and naming `read` for the rest and `edit` for a change in one place. A path of another computer, like `/workspace/notes.txt`: taken from the project folder, and the answer says so. Any other place outside the project: refused, with what the project folder holds. A path ending in .docx, .xlsx, .pptx or .pdf: refused, naming `convert`.

edit.description: Replaces a piece of a file with another, or adds text at the end of a file. To replace: give enough of the old text to find one place only. To add at the end: give `new` alone.

path.description: The file, from the project folder

old.description: The text that is in the file now. Without it: `new` is added after the last line

new.description: The text to put in its place, or to add at the end

all.description: true to replace every place where the old text is. Without it: one place only

edit.answers: `Changed X`, with the lines around the change and their numbers. Without `old`: `Added to X`, with the last lines of the file as they are now; a file that is not there is not created: refused, naming `write`. Old text not found: the lines of the file closest to it, to copy from. Found in more than one place: how many and at which lines, asking for more text or `all`. A path of another computer, like `/workspace/notes.txt`: taken from the project folder, and the answer says so. Any other place outside the project: refused, with what the project folder holds.

search.description: Finds files by their name, or the lines that hold a text, in the project. Give `name`, `text`, or both.

name.description: A pattern for the file name: `*.csv`, `report*`, `**/*.test.ts`

text.description: A text to find inside the files. It returns file, line number and line

folder.description: A folder of the project to search in. Without it: the whole project

search.answers: By name: the paths from the project folder, 100 at most. By text: `path:line: the line`, 100 at most. Nothing found: `Nothing found`, and the folders of the project. Neither `name` nor `text`: refused, saying to give one. A `folder` of another computer, like `/workspace/src`: taken from the project folder, and the answer says so. Any other place outside the project: refused, with what the project folder holds.

web_search.description: Searches the web and returns the results: title, address, date, and a few lines of each. Open the best ones with `web_open` before you answer.

query.description: What to search, in a few words

days.description: Only results of the last days: 7 for a week. Without it: any date

web_search.answers: Ten results at most: title, address, date when known, two lines of text. The first search of a conversation that has not opened the skill `web-research`: the results, then the text of that skill. No network: `The web cannot be reached`, in one line.

web_open.description: Returns the text of a web page. The address comes from a result of `web_search`, from a page you opened, from a file of the project or from the user: never make one up.

url.description: The address, starting with http:// or https://

web_open.answers: The title, the date when known, and the text of the page with the addresses of its links, 300 lines at most. An address that is in no answer of a command and in no message of the user: refused, saying to search first. Not http: refused in one line.

page_view.description: Opens a page in the app's browser and returns what is on it: the text in order, the links, buttons and fields with a number each, and the errors of the console.

page.description: A file of the project, like `page.html`, or an address starting with http

page_view.answers: The title; the text in order; links, buttons and fields with a number each; the errors of the console, or `No errors in the console`. A file that is not there: as `read`.

page_act.description: Clicks, types or presses a key in the page that `page_view` opened, and returns the page as it is afterwards.

on.description: The number `page_view` gave to the link, button or field. Not needed for `press`

text.description: For `type`: the text to write. For `press`: the key, like `Enter`

page_act.answers: The page after the action, as `page_view` gives it. A number that is not on the page: refused, with the numbers that are. No page open: refused, naming `page_view`.

ask.description: Asks the user one question and returns the answer. For a choice only the user can make, or a request that can mean two different things.

question.description: The question, in the user's language

options.description: Two to four answers to choose from. Without it: the user writes freely

ask.answers: What the user answered, as text.

plan.description: Keeps the plan of a long job, for this conversation. `text` writes the whole plan: a document, not a list. `step` with `text` rewrites one step, or adds one, when the work shows that the plan was wrong. `done` says a step is finished and checked, and answers with the whole text of the next step.

done.description: The number of the step you have just finished and checked

text.description:
The plan as a document, in this form:
# Goal
what the user will have at the end
# What is there
the files you read and what each holds, what must not change
## Step 1: a title
everything needed to do this step later without looking again: which files, what to change in each, how to check it
## Step 2: a title
...
# Not doing
what the request does not ask for

step.description: With `text`: the number of the one step to rewrite, or of a new step to add after the last. The rest of the plan and the marks stay as they are

plan.answers: After `text`: the titles of the steps as a list, then the whole text of step 1. A whole plan sent before this conversation has opened the skill `planning`: not kept, and the answer is the text of that skill, asking to send the plan again. A text without `## Step` headings: refused, showing the form. After `step` with `text`: the titles with their marks, and the step as it is now; a step rewritten loses its mark; a number beyond the next free one: refused, with the titles. After `done`: the goal; the titles of the steps, with a mark on those done; then the whole text of the next step, exactly as it was written in the plan. After the last one: `All steps done. Read the goal and Not doing once more, then answer the user`. A `done` for a step that is not there: refused, with the titles. No parameter: the whole plan, or `No plan yet`. An answer to the user while steps are open is held back once, with the open steps. The plan belongs to the conversation: a new conversation starts without one, and the app shows it to the user.
